title: Host compatibility assurance record
description: ADR-0053 §Decision 2 / ADR-0054 §Decision 2 — the human-granted assurance fact carried in the packaged host-parity baseline. STRUCTURE ONLY. Every cross-record and cross-field rule (id uniqueness, negative-wins across duplicate/conflicting/superseded/revoked records, exact package-set equality, ambiguity, vacuous grants, residual coherence, calendar validity) is enforced by lib/assurance-contract.mjs, exactly as runtime-bootstrap-run-1.2 leaves kind exclusivity to lib/evidence-contract.mjs because the validator has no oneOf. Eight semantic cases were measured passing this schema; that is the boundary, not a gap in it. NOTE the `schema` pattern below is an EXACT pin, deliberately diverging from the bootstrap and session families' additive-forward-compat posture (ADR-0054 §Decision 3): a newer minor could add a NARROWING key, and an older reader that ignored it would turn absence of evidence into coverage.

schema.description: Exact pin. `compareSchemaVersion` would accept a newer minor and forgive its unknown scalars; this pattern refuses it first.

grants.description: Append-only. An EMPTY array is the valid, meaningful state of a runtime that ships the gate before any grant exists (ADR-0054 §Decision 6 R1) — every host reads unassured and readiness blocks.

grant.description: One human review decision. A human authors the coverage predicate; runtime only evaluates membership in it (ADR-0053 §Decision 5).

id.description: Immutable identity (ADR-0054 §Decision 8). A revoked grant is never un-revoked, only replaced by a NEW id carrying `reapproval_of`.

state.description: `revoked` is the tombstone §Decision 8 requires to survive a package rollback: removing a positive grant outright is what the cross-tag monotonicity check refuses.

reviewed_at.description: Calendar validity (2026-13-45 is digit-shaped and not a date) is a semantic rule; this pattern fixes the shape only.

review_provenance.description: ADR-0053 §Decision 2/5 — the durable identity of the accepted review. Never a version comparison, and never something runtime derives.

cohort.description: ADR-0053 §Decision 7 — an explicit finite set of reviewed host TUPLES. Per-host lists are deliberately NOT expressible: an array of complete {claude, codex} tuples cannot be read as a Cartesian product, so independent per-host cohorts cannot silently authorize their combinations.

packages.description: ADR-0053 §Decision 8 — the consuming package set and the versions reviewed, because a runtime-packaged grant naming only host versions outlives the code it described. Absence of a package here means it was NOT reviewed, never that it is covered.

predicate.description: ADR-0053 §Decision 5 — extra conditions the reviewer scoped the grant to. Any key runtime cannot observe yields unassured; that judgement belongs to the semantic module, not here.

residuals.description: ADR-0053 §Decision 6 — the open questions the reviewer accepted the host with. Without them assurance is strictly harder to satisfy than exactness and the treadmill merely relocates.

reapproval_of.description: ADR-0054 §Decision 8 — the revoked id this grant re-approves. Recording it as a reference from a NEW id is what keeps revocation append-only.

hostTuple.description: A reviewed host PAIR. The version grammar mirrors host-parity-baseline.mjs's SEMVER_RE — permissive about the core (two components allowed) because this records observed CLI text, strict about prerelease-then-build order because a single [-+] alternative is lossy.

residual.description: ADR-0053 §Decision 6 — a residual on a surface the baseline marks unadopted does not block; one on a CONSUMED surface is the reviewer's call and is recorded as such.
